pathways.name: Move to Cloud Native

findings.finding: Application has no 12-factor compliance: configuration is hardcoded (MongoDB URL, API key, port), not sourced from environment variables.
No graceful shutdown handling. The process has no SIGTERM handler, risking in-flight request loss during container restarts.
No health check endpoint exists in application code. K8s uses TCP socket probes only.
Single-file architecture with no separation of concerns.
No stateless design validation or session externalization.
Application listens on hardcoded port 8080 instead of reading from PORT environment variable.

recommended_actions: Externalize all configuration to environment variables and consume from K8s ConfigMap/Secret
Add a /health endpoint for liveness/readiness probes
Implement graceful shutdown with connection draining
Refactor into modular structure (routes, services, config modules)

pathways.name: Move to Containers

findings.finding: Dockerfile uses node:18-alpine but package.json declares engines node 0.10.x. The --ignore-engines flag papers over incompatibility.
Dockerfile HEALTHCHECK uses wget against /rates which requires API key authentication.
Container security hardening is well-implemented: non-root user, read-only filesystem, dropped capabilities.
K8s manifests follow best practices: resource limits, security contexts, namespace isolation.
No container image scanning or CI/CD pipeline exists.
Image references use latest tag instead of immutable image digests.

recommended_actions: Update package.json engines field to match container runtime (Node 18+)
Fix Dockerfile HEALTHCHECK to target an unauthenticated health endpoint
Use immutable image tags or digests in K8s deployment manifests
Add container image scanning to a CI/CD pipeline

pathways.name: Move to Open Source

findings.finding: Node.js 0.10 is critically EOL (since October 2016). No security patches available. Multiple known CVEs.
Express 3.4.8 is EOL. Uses deprecated express.bodyParser() middleware with known vulnerabilities.
MongoDB native driver 1.4.7 is EOL. Lacks connection pooling, modern auth, and security patches.
No package-lock.json. Dependency resolution is non-deterministic across installs.
Only 2 production dependencies but both have known critical vulnerabilities.
No dependency vulnerability scanning configured.

recommended_actions: Upgrade Node.js runtime to current LTS (Node 20 or 22)
Upgrade Express to version 4.x or 5.x with modern middleware
Upgrade MongoDB driver to 6.x with connection pooling and modern auth
Generate and commit package-lock.json for deterministic builds
Integrate dependency vulnerability scanning

pathways.name: Move to Managed Databases

findings.finding: MongoDB connection string hardcoded to private IP with no authentication. Incompatible with managed services.
No connection pooling. New connection opened and closed for every request.
No database authentication configured. Managed services require credentials.
No TLS/SSL configuration for database connections.
No retry logic or connection error handling beyond generic 500 responses.
Simple query patterns are compatible with DocumentDB MongoDB API compatibility.

recommended_actions: Externalize database connection string to environment variable
Implement connection pooling with modern MongoDB driver
Add TLS/SSL configuration for encrypted connections
Add IAM-based or credential-based authentication compatible with Amazon DocumentDB
Implement connection retry logic with exponential backoff
Evaluate Amazon DocumentDB compatibility for existing query patterns

pathways.name: Move to Managed Analytics

findings.finding: No structured logging. No queryable data produced for analytics pipelines.
No event streaming or message publishing for analytics consumption.
Data could be replicated to analytics layer but no integration exists.
No data pipeline integration. Data locked in MongoDB with no export or CDC mechanism.

recommended_actions: Implement structured JSON logging with business-relevant fields
Consider publishing API events to Amazon EventBridge or Kinesis
Evaluate CDC from MongoDB/DocumentDB for analytics pipelines
Add application metrics for operational analytics

pathways.name: Move to Modern DevOps

findings.finding: No CI/CD pipeline exists. Deployment is manual (git pull + forever restart).
No automated testing of any kind. Zero test coverage.
No infrastructure as code beyond K8s manifests.
No environment separation (dev/staging/prod) configured.
Start script uses forever (not in dependencies) — inappropriate for containers.
No observability pipeline configured.
.gitignore exists with basic Node.js exclusions.

recommended_actions: Implement CI/CD pipeline with build, test, scan, and deploy stages
Add test framework with unit and integration tests
Define infrastructure as code for the runtime environment
Configure environment-specific deployments
Set up observability pipeline
Replace forever with direct node execution

pathways.name: Move to AI

findings.finding: No machine-readable API contract (OpenAPI/Swagger) for AI agent integration.
No structured data output or schema documentation for automated data extraction.
Static pricing formula could be enhanced with ML-based models for dynamic rate optimization.
No data pipeline for historical shipping/quote data to feed ML training.
Simple, well-defined domain suitable for AI augmentation.

recommended_actions: Create OpenAPI 3.x specification for agent and AI tool integration
Consider ML-based pricing models via Amazon SageMaker
Implement data pipelines for model training
Evaluate Amazon Bedrock for natural-language shipping query interfaces

summary.top_priority: Upgrade EOL runtime and dependencies (Node.js, Express, MongoDB driver) to establish a secure, supported foundation for all other modernization efforts.
